summary: Intro discovery for Mesonic Labs evaluating Redwood's PLG quickstart and hosted vs dedicated options. They care about time-to-first-token, free credits for evaluation, and security (SOC2, SSO, KMS). SE to run benchmarks and Samir to send quickstart links and credits instructions.

Benchmarking and cost per token / latency
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE for this region. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Aisha: Aisha here, CTO at Mesonic. Marcus and Priyanka on the call too.
[00:10] Marcus: Hey.
[00:12] Priyanka: hi all.
[00:15] Samir: Great. Lena from our SE team is with me, she'll do a bit of a tech deep dive if we need it.
[00:20] Lena: Hi all, thanks for having us.
[00:24] Samir: Cool, high level agenda, we want to understand your use case, current stack, success criteria, and then talk through the Redwood quickstart path — free credits, time-to-first-token, and deployment options.
[00:34] Aisha: Perfect. For context, we are building an internal dev assistant that surfaces code snippets and runbook answers, mostly text generation and embeddings for search. Privacy is important; some datasets are internal only. We're evaluating hosted APIs first for speed to production, but we'll likely need dedicated pools for predictable latency.
[00:50] Samir: Makes sense. Marcus, what's your current infra?
[00:54] Marcus: Right now we're using managed endpoints from another vendor, and self-hosted for a few models on prem. Latency is okay but costs balloon during heavy usage. We want predictable unit economics — cost per token and tail latency.
[01:07] Lena: Understood. For the quickstart, the hosted Redwood API is plg-friendly — you sign up, get free credits, API keys, and can be sending your first token in under 10 minutes. The quickstart docs include a sample curl and SDK snippet.
[01:21] Marcus: Ten minutes, that's optimistic but good. How do free credits and quota limits look?
[01:26] Samir: Typically we grant evaluation credits that cover several thousand requests depending on model choice — the credits page summarizes model-specific units. For PLG signups there are per-minute rate limits till we bump you up, but we can expedite if you want sustained throughput for benchmark runs.
[01:40] Priyanka: Do you require a company email? Any SSO gating for the trial?
[01:44] Samir: For credits we usually validate company domain. No mandatory SSO for the quickstart; SSO/SAML integration comes later for enterprise accounts.
[01:51] Aisha: Security is big for us. We need SOC2 type II, audit logs, KMS integration for customer keys, and network isolation if we move to private. What's Redwood's posture?
[02:03] Lena: Redwood is SOC 2 compliant, we provide audit logs, and for Private/Dedicated we support bringing your own KMS/HSM and VPC peering options. There's also an on-prem package for air-gapped needs. For hosted customers we encrypt at rest and in transit — customer-managed keys are possible on Dedicated/Private.
[02:23] Marcus: Are logs accessible? We need per-request tracing to correlate model outputs to our app logs for debugging.
[02:29] Lena: Yes we expose per-request tracing in the Console; token-level latency and cost breakdown. You can pull logs via our API or stream to a SIEM.
[02:38] Aisha: Good. On the model side, we care about latency at 99th percentile under our typical request size (avg 350 tokens). Can we run benchmarks?
[02:47] Samir: Absolutely. Typical flow is quickstart on hosted to validate quality and integrate, then SE-led benchmark on dedicated capacity if you want throughput and stricter SLOs. Lena, we can run a 2-hour benchmark with their sample set.
[02:59] Lena: Yep, if you share the 10k sample queries and QPS profile we can replicate and send back latency/cost numbers, also test quantized variants to reduce cost.
[03:10] Marcus: Cool. A few technical clarifications — how does Redwood handle KV cache and prefix caching across requests? We want to avoid re-forwarding long contexts frequently.
[03:20] Lena: The runtime supports KV cache reuse and prefix caching; for hosted we do automatic prefix caching and continuous batching to improve throughput. Note the KV cache is per-session and we expose APIs for warm-up.
[03:33] Marcus: And for private deployments is the behavior identical?
[03:36] Lena: The runtime is the same across modes; differences are in networking and KMS. In Dedicated/Private you can pin model versions and control autoscaling policies.
[03:46] Aisha: Pricing — ballpark cost per token or per 1k tokens for the models you recommend?
[03:52] Samir: For open quantized models we're competitive — costs vary by model and quantization. We can share a sample cost sheet; for quickstart we usually recommend starting with a mid-sized open model for iteration, then move to a larger model or a distillation for scale.
[04:06] Priyanka: Does Redwood support streaming responses and function calling? We need streaming for UX.
[04:11] Lena: Yes streaming and tool-calls are supported. Structured output with JSON schemas is also supported via the SDKs.
[04:19] Marcus: On the PLG side, how long between signup and getting a token that actually returns real responses? We've had trials where the initial API returns a 503 while infra warms up.
[04:28] Samir: In our experience, if you use the quickstart flow and pick a hosted model you'll get first successful generative response typically under 5-15 minutes. There's some variability due to cold-starts and region. We offer warm pools and you can request reserved warm instances if you want consistent low-latency from day one.
[04:46] Aisha: For our evaluation we want to: 1) get a developer on-boarding flow working in the next week, 2) run a benchmark for latency/cost, 3) evaluate Dedicated for production. Timeline-wise we want a pilot in production in 6-8 weeks.
[05:03] Samir: That sounds reasonable. We'll get you credits and the quickstart link today, SE to run the benchmark and then a decision on Dedicated sizing after results.
[05:11] Marcus: One last question — data retention and deletion. We cannot allow customer PII to be used for training external models.
[05:17] Lena: By default hosted transient logs are retained for monitoring and audit but we have options to disable training usage; enterprise contracts include clauses for data not being used for training and specific retention windows. For Private/Dedicated you control the data plane.
[05:30] Priyanka: Great. Could you send over SOC 2, DPA, and a sample contract?
[05:34] Samir: Yep I'll attach those. Lena, anything else on tech?
[05:38] Lena: Just to confirm the sample sizes and QPS, and whether you'll want to test quantized model paths vs float. Also we'll show examples of batching config and autoscale policies.
[05:49] Marcus: We'll provide queries and target 50 QPS for the benchmark.
[05:53] Samir: Perfect, we'll aim to schedule the benchmark early next week.
[05:57] Aisha: Thanks everyone, this is good.
[06:00] Samir: Quick recap — Samir send quickstart link + free credits guide, Lena schedule benchmark and bring dedicated config, Mesonic share 10k sample and QPS profile. Any other blockers?
[06:12] Priyanka: None from product side.
[06:14] Marcus: No.
[06:15] Samir: Alright we'll follow up with next steps. Thanks all.
[06:20] (call ends)
notes: Mentions of KV cache sometimes transcribed as 'K V cash' or 'K V cache' in the automated transcript; some speaker labels were generic and manually corrected.
